$description: TE dark is a Teenage Engineering-inspired dark theme, the night twin of TE calm. TE calm is the reference. Each value must meet these targets. Tint and dE values are CAM16-UCS on the TE dark base, and the tint thresholds come from side-by-side reading tests. (1) Readable: body text is about 10:1 on the base, and each code role is at least 8:1. (2) Frequent code looks like text: functions, variables, symbols, punctuation, constants, and links are tinted text. Links keep their underline: tint at most about 6, the distance from a neutral gray of the same lightness. (3) One hue in code: strings, and the keywords that share their color, are the only code role with a visible hue: tint about 11 to 15. Below 7 the hue disappears; above 17 the code looks like fireworks. (4) Important things stand out: comments, search matches, selections, and diagnostics are visible at a glance. Their backgrounds are at least about 5 dE from the base, and search and selection at least about 15. (5) One loud color: only error and attention marks use the saturated alert red. (6) Twin of TE calm: each role keeps TE calm's hue and its rank of visibility. (7) Color vision deficiency: error and warning, added and deleted lines, and search and selection differ in lightness, at least about 7 dE with deuteranopia. Judge changes in dark mode after about 5 minutes, side by side on several files, and with a blur test.

ink.$description: Tinted text for code, measured in CAM16-UCS on the base. cool, blue, and violet are near-neutral (tint about 5), so frequent code reads as text. green is the only visible code hue (tint about 13). The other scales still supply the ANSI and status colors.

semantic.$description: Layer 2 assigns meaning to the primitive colors. Each value refers to a primitive color or to another role. Gray carries the interface. Blue marks information, functions, interface accents, selections, and changed lines. Green marks strings, additions, and success. Red marks errors and deletions. Amber marks warnings and search. Cyan on plum marks comments. Violet marks constants and matching brackets.

surface.$description: Gray backgrounds from the neutral scale.

base.$description: Shared neutral background for the editor, terminal, and Zellij.

raised.$description: Background for bars and panels: the status line, the tab bar, and unfocused windows.

cursorline.$description: Background for the current line. One step above the base marks the line without washing out strings.

highlight.$description: Background for tab hover and Zellij indicator fills. Selected entries use selection.secondary.

ruler.$description: Background for the line-length ruler: Helix rulers and Neovim colorcolumn.

popup.$description: Background for popups, menus, floating windows, and Telescope. One step above the base background distinguishes the window area from its border.

active.$description: Background for the active Neovim and Helix tab. mode.normal aliases it. The gray keycap with light text is calmer than a white block.

current.$description: Background for the current WezTerm and Zellij tab. The dark accent tint with text.accent marks where you are without a heavy block.

default.$description: Color for split separators, the scrollbar, and borders.

subtle.$description: Color for unfocused Zellij pane frames and titles. Fainter than border.default, so the focused frame in text.accent is the only clear outline.

text.$description: Foreground colors for interface and body text.

secondary.$description: Foreground for secondary text and status text.

muted.$description: Foreground for hints, line numbers, and secondary interface text.

accent.$description: Foreground for interface elements that need a color: the current line number, directories, and key hints. blue.700 is lighter and more saturated than syntax.function (blue.600), so interface text does not look like a function name.

strong.$description: Foreground for the backgrounds with the most emphasis: the current search match, the active tab, and mode keycaps.

syntax.$description: Code colors. Interface elements do not use them; they use text.accent and status.*.

string.$description: Foreground for string literals and the keywords that share their color. ink.green is the only visible hue in code, slightly darker than body text.

constant.$description: Foreground for constants, numbers, and booleans. ink.violet is near-neutral and lighter than body text, so constants differ from functions in lightness, not hue.

function.$description: Foreground for function names. Function names are the most frequent code role, so ink.cool is near-neutral: it reads as text with a cool tint.

link.$description: Foreground for links and URLs. ink.blue is near-neutral, like the link color in TE calm. The underline carries the signal.

status.$description: Foreground colors for diagnostics and state.

error.$description: Foreground for error messages and diagnostic text.

warning.$description: Foreground for warnings. amber.500 is darker than status.error (red.700), so the two differ in lightness as well as hue.

hint.$description: Foreground for hints. It aliases text.muted.

success.$description: Foreground for success states and Git additions.

errorMark.$description: Foreground for the curved error underline and bold sign glyph. This is the only high-saturation color. Diagnostic messages use status.error. Do not use it as a background.

signal.$description: Small marks that must stand out.

mark.$description: Small mark for an unsaved buffer, an active macro recording, or the Zellij bell. It uses the saturated alert red. Do not use it as a background or for anything else.

selection.$description: Backgrounds for selections and related matches.

secondary.$description: Background for inactive selections and for the selected entry in menus, pickers, lists, and file explorers. gray.300 is two steps above the popup, so the entry stays visible on near-black.

match.$description: Background for matching brackets and LSP references. violet.200 stays visible on the current line (gray.100), where violet.100 would disappear.
Background for all search matches. The amber background steps are warmed toward orange, because dark yellow looks olive.

current.$description: Background for the current search match and jump labels, one step above search.match with more chroma.

comment.$description: Code comments: a cyan foreground on a dark plum background.

markerBg.$description: Background for TODO, FIXME, WARNING, and NOTE markers. plum.200 is one step above the comment background.

doc.$description: Documentation comments and Markdown. Names that end in Bg are backgrounds; the others are foregrounds.

bg.$description: Background for documentation comments and docstrings. It aliases comment.bg for now.

quoteBg.$description: Background for blockquotes and the Octo editing area. blue.100 is visible against the base background, where blue.50 is not.

codeBg.$description: Background for inline code and fenced code blocks.

diff.$description: Backgrounds for added, changed, and deleted lines, and for changed words. Line tints use step N and changed words use step N+1.

changeWord.$description: Background for changed words inside changed lines, one step above diff.change.

primary.$description: Primary cursor background. Its near-white color distinguishes the cursor from the text background.

mode.$description: Backgrounds for the mode keycap in the status line. Each mode uses light text (text.strong) on a dark tint, so the keycap shape stays the same and only the tint changes.

normal.$description: Normal mode. It aliases surface.active, the gray keycap.

insert.$description: Insert mode. Green relates to additions.

select.$description: Select mode in Helix and Visual mode in Neovim. It aliases selection.primary, so the keycap matches the selection.

replace.$description: Replace mode (Neovim). Red relates to deletion, because replace overwrites text.

terminal.$description: ANSI palette for terminals. black (gray.300) stays visible on the base, and bright.white (gray.900) stays lighter than white (gray.700) to keep the ANSI order. The default terminal foreground uses text.primary.
